title: On the limited memory BFGS method for large scale optimization
contribution: Second (OCR) read of the 1989 L-BFGS study (round-1 card c01, prose only): the table numbers are now legible. They show L-BFGS beating Buckley-LeNir on evaluations, scaling M3 cutting evaluations against M1 on every legible row, and n = 5000-10000 solved in 14-183 iterations. PQN needs fewer evaluations in 35 of 38 runs (my count), but wins clearly on time on one problem only (Tables 3-4, 8-9, 11, 14, 18-19; pp. 9-21).
problem_entry: As in c01: no comparison of limited-memory methods with each other since Gill-Murray 1979, little known against Newton or PQN on large problems (p. 3). New: 16 test problems with n from 49 to 10000, sources listed in Table 1 (pp. 6-7).
key_idea: Algorithm 2.1: BFGS with a Wolfe search (0 < beta' < 1/2, beta' < beta < 1), unit step first, H_k from min{k, m-1}+1 updates of H0 (p. 5). Scalings now legible (p. 14): M1 none; M2 gamma0 = y0's0/||y0||^2 once (3.2); M3 gamma_k = y_k's_k/||y_k||^2 every iteration (4.1); M4 a diagonal D_k minimizing ||D_k Y_{k-1} - S_{k-1}||_F over the last m steps, safeguarded, falling back to gamma_k (4.2)-(4.3). Test search: strong-Wolfe form (3.1) with beta' = 1e-4 and beta = 0.9, the Buckley-LeNir values (p. 8). The accurate variant forces one cubic interpolation (p. 12). The analysis uses the equivalent Algorithm 6.1 (p. 22).
assumptions: Assumptions 6.1: f in C^2, convex level set, M1||z||^2 <= z'G(x)z <= M2||z||^2 on D (6.4) (p. 22); {B_k^(0)} and their inverses bounded (p. 23). Tests: low-accuracy stop relative to max(1,||x_k||) (exponent garbled) (p. 7); H0 = I, then gamma0 I (p. 8); SUN 3/60 in double precision (p. 8); Alliant FX/8 for n = 5000, 10000 (p. 15).
proof_devices: Theorem 6.1: for any positive definite B0, x_k -> x* and f_k - f* <= r^k (f0 - f*), 0 <= r < 1 (6.5) (p. 23)
averaged Hessian y_k = Gbar_k s_k gives M1||s||^2 <= y's <= M2||s||^2 (6.8) and ||y||^2/y's <= M2 (6.9) (p. 23)
uniform trace bound tr(B_{k+1}) <= tr(B_k^(0)) + m~ M2 <= M3 (6.10) and Pearson/Powell determinant bound det(B_{k+1}) >= M4 (6.11)-(6.12) give cos theta_k >= delta (6.13) (pp. 23-24)
Powell's decrease inequality f_{k+1} - f* <= (1 - c cos^2 theta_k)(f_k - f*) gives (6.5); (1/2)M1||x_k - x*||^2 <= f_k - f* gives R-linear iterates (p. 24)
gamma_k bounded by constants from (6.4), (6.9), so M3 meets the theorem; Shanno-Phua and Buckley-LeNir are special cases; R-linear is the best possible for L-BFGS (p. 24)
experiments: Table 3 (B-L vs L-BFGS, m = 5, 7, 9, p. 9). Problem 1 (n = 1000): 19/88-19/75 against 45/55-44/54. Problem 10 (n = 961): 171/343-172/346 against 168/280-163/267, total times 1308-1407 against 1146-1290. B-L needs fewer iterations but about two evaluations each. Table 4 (m = 15 and BFGS, p. 9): BFGS usually fewest calls, e.g. problem 12: 229/464, 263/269, 179/185. Speed-up NFUN(3)/NFUN(7): L-BFGS substantial in 70% of problems, B-L little (p. 11). Table 8: gains beyond m = 15 small and not monotone (p. 12). Table 9: a forced interpolation cuts iterations (problem 1: 44-45 -> 16) and raises evaluations (problem 12: 251-260 -> 447-461) (pp. 9, 12). Table 11 (m = 5; M1/M2/M3/M4, p. 14): problem 10 569/280/197/179 evaluations; problem 11 83/42/22/22, times 183/153/63/74. M3 beats M1 on every legible row but loses to M2 on problem 12 (322 against 260 evaluations, 293 against 238 time). M4 safeguard used in about 5% of iterations (p. 15). Table 14 (M3, n = 5000/10000, p. 16): 14-183 iterations. Tables 18-19 (PQN vs L-BFGS M3, m = 5, pp. 19-20): problem 9 PQN time 53/62 against 1608; problem 10 with variable reduction 853/854 against 964, without 3479/1439 against 964; dense problem 12 PQN 14871/21290 against 293. PQN iteration 2-5x, on problems 10 and 15 10-15x, L-BFGS's (p. 21). Illegible: Tables 2, 5-7, 10, 12-13, 16-17, 20 and the headers of 9, 14, 15.
positioning: As in c01; for given m the two limited-memory methods need roughly the same storage, L-BFGS slightly less arithmetic (p. 7); Gilbert-Lemarechal used Buckley's newer 1987 code and found smaller differences (p. 4); PQN highly recommended when the element functions depend on fewer than 4 or 5 variables (p. 24).
writing: Numeric user advice for VA15: low storage and accurate searches for cheap functions; 3 <= m <= 7 (page image of p. 18; the OCR prints <) with an inaccurate search for expensive ones (p. 18). Overlapping thresholds in the final remarks (PQN below 4 or 5 element variables; L-BFGS can be faster above 3 or 4, p. 24). Numbering slip: section 7 carries Algorithm/Assumptions/Theorem 6.1 (pp. 21-23).
limits_future: R-linear is the best possible (p. 24); storage gains at n = 5000-10000 marginal and unexplained, iteration counts small multiples of m (p. 16); CG competitive for large cheap problems (pp. 18, 25); dynamic scaling as the main future topic (p. 15).

method_links.note: Refines c01 (one piece of evidence): rival at defaults with its authors' constants beta' = 1e-4, beta = 0.9, used by L-BFGS too; same-solution check for every run; count and split-time lines; loss to PQN in the abstract and in full in Tables 18-19.

SKILL Method 1 step 5 and catalog E2 cite S002 p. 8 for dropping problems with different solutions and counting them per code; the text only verifies that both methods reached the same solution in each run, with no drop and no count. Also as c01: the alignment move upgrades the own line search (Table 9).

PQN recommended over the own method, with numbers: PQN fewer evaluations in 35 of 38 runs (exceptions: problem 3 from the finite-difference start, problem 14 at n = 100 from the scaled-identity start; page images); time win on problem 9 (53-62 vs 1608), tie on problem 10 with variable reduction (853 vs 964), loss without it (3479/1439 vs 964); iteration cost 2-5x (10-15x on two problems); less attractive above 4 or 5 element variables; misapplied on dense problem 12 (14871 vs 293).

The two line-search options rest on Table 9: forcing an interpolation cuts iterations and raises evaluations. Also Heuristic 5 (M3 over M4, M4 safeguard 5% of iterations, m-ranges per cost regime matching the code's 3<= M <=7) and Heuristic 4 (Gill-Murray scaling dropped).
As c01: Theorem 6.1 covers Shanno-Phua and Buckley-LeNir too, and the rival can be made n-step quadratic; it does not discriminate.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: storage-matched head-to-head with a structured rival, including a deliberately misapplied case
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Stg, it/nf and split times per method in one row; the dense-Hessian problem kept to show PQN misapplied; continues c01's cost-split reporting candidate

transferable: Print storage, iterations/evaluations and iteration/function/total time per method in one row, so a win on one count and a tie on another show together (pp. 19-20).
Give storage advice as a range tied to the cost regime: cheap functions get low storage and accurate searches; expensive ones get 3-7 corrections and an inexact search (p. 18).
Report how often each safeguard fires (M4: about 5% of iterations) (p. 15).
Measure the value of extra storage as NFUN(m1)/NFUN(m2) and show its distribution over the test set (pp. 10-11).
Label each variant with a one-line formula (M1-M4) before tallying (p. 14).
coauthors: Dong C. Liu (Northwestern EECS); Richard Byrd suggested scaling M4 (acknowledged, p. 25)

quotes.text: In contrast, the L-BFGS method gives a substantial speed-up in 70% of the problems.
We observe large variations in the iteration time of PQN: for most problems it is 2 to 5 times larger than that of L-BFGS.

title: Theory of algorithms for unconstrained optimization
contribution: Second (OCR) read of the Acta Numerica survey (round-1 card c02): theorem statements, constants and the targeted-run numbers are now legible. BFGS 15 iterations against DFP 4041 (close to Powell's estimate) and phi = 0.999 at 2223; sigma1 = 1e-4, sigma2 = 0.9; m in [3,7]; the Khalfan-Byrd-Schnabel SR1 rate is 2n-step q-quadratic (pp. 17, 24, 29, 31).
problem_entry: As in c02 (a user's view of which theory matters, methods as implemented, pp. 1-2). New: progress 'in the last 15 years' (p. 1); trust-region theory obtained before 1982, hence omitted (p. 3); large n fixed as 10,000 to justify studying unrestarted CG (p. 11).
key_idea: Four classes of results and a few hub principles (pp. 2, 4-7). Settings now legible: BFGS with a very loose search, sigma1 = 1e-4, sigma2 = 0.9 (pp. 16-17); the unit trial step always, since alpha = 1 satisfies Wolfe for large k if sigma1 < 1/2 (p. 7); PR+ beta = max{beta_PR, 0} (4.8) (p. 13); L-BFGS with m in [3,7] (p. 31); library list tied to codes VA14, CONMIN, IMSL/NAG BFGS, VE08, VA15, Nash's truncated Newton, IMSL Nelder-Mead for noisy functions (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: Theorem 3.1: f bounded below, C^1 near the level set, Lipschitz gradient L, Wolfe steps 0 < sigma1 < sigma2 < 1 (pp. 4-5). Strong convexity m||z||^2 <= z'Gz <= M||z||^2 (5.6) (p. 18). Theorem 5.1: any pairs with y's/s's >= m (5.18), ||y||^2/y's <= M (5.19) (p. 21). CGT SR1: C^2, bounded Lipschitz Hessian, (6.2) with r in (0,1), uniformly independent steps (p. 28); KBS replace independence by bounded positive definite B_k (p. 29). Powell 1986: two-variable quadratic, G(x*) = I, unit steps (p. 23).
proof_devices: Zoutendijk sum cos^2 theta_k ||g_k||^2 < inf (3.9) from alpha_k >= ((sigma2-1)/L) g'd/||d||^2 (3.10) and c = sigma1(sigma2-1)/L; cond(B_k) <= A gives cos theta_k >= 1/A (pp. 5-6)
steepest descent on a quadratic: f_{k+1} <= [(lambda_n - lambda_1)/(lambda_n + lambda_1)]^2 f_k via Kantorovich (3.21); same constant asymptotically with one quadratic interpolation (pp. 8-9)

CG: Al-Baali sufficient descent g'd <= -c||g||^2 (4.7); |beta| <= beta_FR suffices and c > 1 is tight (Gilbert-Nocedal); Theorem 4.2 (beta >= 0, (4.7), Property (*)) gives liminf ||g|| = 0; n-step quadratic rates (Cohen, Burmeister, Ritter) (pp. 11-14)

BFGS trace and determinant: ||s|| <= c2||g|| cos theta with c2 = 2(1-sigma1)/m (5.9), decrease term ~ alpha/cos^2 theta (5.10), increase term <= M (5.13), det(B_{k+1}) = det(B_k) y's/s'Bs (5.15); Broyden-class decrease term ~ 1/cos^2 theta against an uncertain-sign term ~ 1/cos theta (5.16)-(5.17) (pp. 18-20)
Theorem 5.1 (Byrd-Nocedal 1989): for any p in (0,1), cos theta_j >= beta1 for at least ceil(pk) of j in [1,k]; psi(B) = tr(B) - ln det(B) >= ln cond(B) (5.21) (p. 21)
Theorem 5.2 (Powell 1976a): BFGS liminf ||g|| = 0 if ||y||^2/y's stays bounded (5.22) (p. 22)
Powell 1986: DFP iterations of order lambda_1 for a large initial eigenvalue, BFGS logarithmic in lambda_1 in the worst case (pp. 23-24)
SR1: n+1-step termination on strongly convex quadratics (Fiacco-McCormick, p. 27); B_k -> Hessian (CGT, p. 28); 2n-step q-quadratic, limsup e_{k+2n}/e_k^2 < inf (KBS, p. 29), correcting c02's n-step
trust regions: ||B_k|| growing at most linearly suffices; an accumulation point with zero gradient and PSD Hessian (p. 32)
experiments: No new experiments; the reported targeted runs now have numbers. Byrd-Nocedal-Yuan two-variable test (quadratic plus small quartic, start eigenvalues 1 and 1e4): BFGS solved in 15 iterations, trace 1e4 -> 3 in 10 iterations; DFP 4041 iterations (close to Powell's estimate), 3000 iterations to bring the trace to 1100; phi = 0.999 needed 2223 (p. 24). FR on the 961-variable minimal surface makes tiny steps for hundreds of iterations (p. 12). CG family storage FR 4, PR 5, VE04 6, CONMIN 7 n-vectors, evaluation ranking in the same order (p. 15). KBS: in about one third of problems neither SR1 nor BFGS approximates the Hessian well (p. 28). Zhang-Tewarson negative phi: moderate but consistent gain (p. 25).
positioning: As in c02. Open Question I on DFP unanswered since 1976, for a method known for almost 30 years (pp. 17-18). L-BFGS said to be competitive with PQN when element functions have more than 5 or 6 variables, citing Liu-Nocedal 1989 (p. 30), while the 1989 study itself prints 3-5 [S002 pp. 21, 24]: a drift between source and survey.
writing: Numbers serve as argument anchors: n = 10,000 for the unrestarted-CG regime (p. 11), three counts (15, 4041, 2223) for the BFGS-DFP story (p. 24), a storage ladder 4-5-6-7 for CG extensions (p. 15). Otherwise as c02.
limits_future: As c02, now dated: DFP convergence open since 1976 (p. 17); why L-BFGS with m in [3,7] is as fast as BFGS on many problems is not understood (p. 31); no counterexample for nonconvex BFGS yet (p. 22).

method_links.note: Refines c02 (one piece of evidence): the separating mechanism is confirmed by a targeted run whose count is set against the theoretical estimate (DFP 4041 against BFGS 15, close to Powell's estimate), and the continuity question is answered by running phi = 0.999 (2223); steps 2 and 4 in a 1992 survey. Also Taste mark 4 quantified (trace 1e4 -> 3 in 10 BFGS iterations; DFP 3000 iterations to 1100).
As c02: PQN one of the major algorithmic advances; CG best for very large problems with cheap functions.
The survey restates the L-BFGS/PQN crossover as more than 5 or 6 element variables, where the cited 1989 study prints 3-5 (S002 pp. 21, 24); a skill statement of the threshold should cite S002.

As c02: angle tests rejected by argument and by what the best codes do, not by a new experiment. Also Heuristic 5: parameter advice as numbers (sigma1 = 1e-4, sigma2 = 0.9, unit trial step, m in [3,7]).

transferable: Put the theory's predicted count next to the observed count on one small, nearly quadratic problem, and say how close they are (p. 24).
Answer a continuity question (holds at phi = 0.999, why not at 1?) with the run at 0.999 as well as with the argument (pp. 18, 24).
Rank a family of methods by storage and by evaluations in one sentence, to show the extra vectors buy the gain (p. 15).
Fix the scale of 'large' with a number (n = 10,000) before arguing which theoretical regime matters (p. 11).
coauthors: none (single-authored); thanks Marucha Lalee, Christy Hartung, Peihuang Lu

quotes.text: In contrast, the DFP method required 4041 iterations to obtain the solution (which is amazingly close to the estimate given by Powell).
Then the rate of convergence is 2n-step q-quadratic

title: Representations of quasi-Newton matrices and their use in limited memory methods
contribution: Second (OCR) read of the compact-representation paper (round-1 card c02; TR NAM-03, June 1992, revised January 21, 1996). The formulas and the multiplication counts are now legible: unconstrained step 4mn + O(m^2) = the two-loop recursion's 4mn; H_k e_i 2mn + O(m^2) against (4m-1)n; reduced-Hessian work (4m+1)t; compact update 2mn against (3/2)m^2 n (pp. 13, 15, 17-20).
problem_entry: As in c02 (projections and the direct matrix are expensive with the recursion, pp. 2, 4). New: m in [3,7] suffices in practice (p. 3); the recursion's H_k e_i costs (4m-1)n, almost the dense cost, and no O(mn) recursion exists for B_k (p. 19).
key_idea: Lemma 2.1: V0...V_{k-1} = I - Y_k R_k^{-1} S_k', R_k upper triangular of s_{i-1}'y_{j-1} (2.2)-(2.3) (p. 5). Theorem 2.2: inverse compact form (2.6) with D_k = diag(s_i'y_i) (2.7) (p. 6). Theorem 2.3: direct form (2.17) with L_k strictly lower (2.18) (p. 7), L_k = S_k'Y_k - R_k (2.22) (p. 8). Theorem 2.4: S'B0S + L D^{-1} L' positive definite, so only a k x k Cholesky is needed (p. 9). Limited memory with H^(0) = gamma_k I (3.1), B^(0) = sigma_k I (3.5) (p. 10), gamma_k (3.12) and sigma_k (3.23) (pp. 12, 16). SR1 forms (5.2), (5.9) (pp. 21-22); Broyden forms (6.4), (6.15) (pp. 23, 25).
assumptions: BFGS: s_i'y_i > 0 and a positive definite start (pp. 6-7); SR1: a well-defined update (p. 21); Broyden: nonzero s_i, nonsingular start (pp. 23, 25); scalar basic matrix 'because this choice is common in practice' (p. 10); m constant (p. 9); m very small in practice, 'say m < 7' in the OCR (p. 11).
proof_devices: induction with the bordered triangular R_{k+1} for the product of projections (p. 5)
split H_k = M_k + N_k, N_k = S_k R_k^{-T} D_k R_k^{-1} S_k' (2.12) by induction (pp. 6-7)
Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury through the explicit inverse of the middle matrix C_k (2.20) to get the direct form (p. 8)
positive definiteness of S'B0S + L D^{-1} L' by contradiction through triangular R_k with positive diagonal (p. 9)
two-loop coefficients equal R_k^{-1} S_k' g_k; the recursion is the adjoint of g -> (1/2) g'H_k g (p. 19)
exact equivalence with multiple secant updates: Y'S = D (conjugate directions) for BFGS (p. 26); symmetry s_i'y_j = s_j'y_i for SR1 (p. 28)
experiments: n/a (no tests). Multiplication counts now legible: Algorithm 3.1 (2m+1)n + (2m+1)n + O(m^2) = (4m+2)n + O(m^2), extra work 4mn + O(m^2) inside a line-search code (p. 13); two-loop recursion 4mn (+ n for diagonal H0) (p. 18). H_k v (4m+1)n + 3m^2 (p. 13); v'H_k v (2m+1)n + O(m^2), roughly half (p. 14); u'H_k v (4m+1)n + 2m^2 + O(m) against (4m+2)n + O(m^2) (p. 14). A'H_kA: 2mnt for S'A, Y'A; other products (2t+4m)n (pp. 14-15). Sparse: H_k e_i 2mn + O(m^2), e_i'H_k e_i O(m^2), work proportional to nonzeros n_A (p. 15), against (4m-1)n for the two-loop recursion (p. 19). B_k: forming 2mn plus lower order, B_k v (4m+1)n + O(m^2), v'B_k v (2m+1)n + O(m^2), B_k e_i 2mn + O(m^2) (pp. 16-17); reduced Hessian product (4m+1)t + O(m^2), theta'B theta (2m+1)t + O(m^2) (pp. 17-18). gamma_k free, sigma_k one multiplication (pp. 13, 16). Straightforward direct approach (3/2)m^2 n to form against 2mn (p. 20).
positioning: As in c02. The two-loop recursion is kept as better when H^(0) is not a scalar multiple of I (pp. 18-19); no O(mn) direct recursion known (p. 19); multiple secant BFGS not advantageous (p. 27), Broyden preference not clear cut (p. 28). Users dated: Mahidhara-Lasdon 1990, Byrd-Lu-Nocedal 1993 (p. 16), Biegler-Nocedal-Schmid 1993 (p. 25).
writing: Each algorithm box ends with per-step counts and a total (pp. 13, 16-17); every comparative word is backed by two counts ('roughly half', 'only slightly less expensive', p. 14; 'less efficient', p. 20); hedge 'as far as we know' on parity (p. 13).
limits_future: No numerical tests; no gain over the recursion for unconstrained problems (pp. 13, 18); recursion preferable for non-scalar H^(0) (pp. 18-19); SR1 skip test can be expensive, triangular factorization of M_k suggested (p. 23); no detailed limited-memory SR1 algorithms (p. 23).

method_links.note: As c02 (one piece of evidence): matrix kept, representation replaced; parity with the incumbent on its home problem now exact, 4mn + O(m^2) against the two-loop recursion's 4mn.
As c02, with counts: structure exploited inside the generic method's linear algebra; H_k e_i 2mn + O(m^2) against (4m-1)n; reduced-Hessian work in t rather than n.

Step 5 (record where each part loses): the incumbent two-loop recursion is kept as the better choice for a non-scalar H^(0). Also Heuristic 5 with exact counts (gamma_k free, sigma_k one multiplication, (3/2)m^2 n against 2mn), confirming 08 and catalog D2 [S014 pp. 12-13, 19-20]; Heuristic 7 staircase users dated.

transferable: State the incumbent's exact cost for the same operation next to yours, and claim parity only when the leading terms agree (4mn and 4mn) (pp. 13, 18).
Separate the cost of forming a representation from the cost of using it (2mn to form B_k, (4m+1)n for B_k v), so a comparison can be won on formation alone ((3/2)m^2 n against 2mn) (pp. 16-17, 20).
Choose free parameters (gamma_k, sigma_k) by what is already stored, so they cost nothing or one multiplication (pp. 13, 16).
Write the product of rank-one projections in closed form once (Lemma 2.1); every compact form then follows by induction or Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (pp. 5-8, 23-25).
coauthors: Richard H. Byrd, Robert B. Schnabel (University of Colorado, Boulder); thanks Peihuang Lu

quotes.text: Of course for large problems the term 4mn predominates.
updating the representation of the limited memory matrix using the compact form requires only 2mn multiplications, compared to 3/2 … multiplications needed by the approach described in this section.
